Format and lint the existing FFT modules before the optional FFT behavior changes.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: formatting, import-order and lint cleanup.

This change affects: existing NumPy, CuPy, cuFFT and FFT backend/CLI dispatch modules.

This change changes: source presentation, import ordering, explicit public re-exports and the traceback context of an optional-import error. No dependencies are added.

This change: uses the pinned formatter and includes a structural comparison and the validation recorded below.

This change will: preserve the dependency scope described above.

## Motivation

Separating formatting from the optional FFT changes makes the batching fixes and FFTW wisdom lifecycle easier to review.

## Contents

Pinned Ruff 0.14.6 formatting and I001 import ordering in five existing files: `pycbc/fft/__init__.py`, `cufft.py`, `cupyfft.py`, `npfft.py` and `parser_support.py`. Import names are preserved. Batch execution, cache keys, wisdom handling and new tests stay in the feature PR. The existing public-export aliases and optional-import exception context are made explicit here to satisfy the static checks.

This replacement head retains the formatting changes, marks the existing FFT public re-exports explicitly, and suppresses the redundant exception context for the existing optional cuFFT import error. It inherits the performance, executable-context and precision fixes from [#15](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/15) at `2685db817fe0fdb77de2e0196fbdfd66d4faf713`. Those fixes are outside this PR’s own diff.

## Links to any issues or associated PRs

Depends on [#15](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/15) (`torch-pr11-performance-evidence`) at `2685db817fe0fdb77de2e0196fbdfd66d4faf713` and precedes [#16](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/16). This optional formatting branch is outside the main stack; [#17](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/17) remains an independent child of [#15](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/15) and needs no formatting prerequisite.

Head branch: `torch-fft-formatting-base`. Head commit: `a0506820e0689a30903d6b28efd7c4f47e5110cf`. Base branch: `torch-pr11-performance-evidence`.

body:
Add optional CPU acceleration for Torch search workloads.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: efficiency update and bug fixes.

This change affects: Torch-backed PyCBC workflows in the areas described below, with CPU compatibility coverage.

This change changes: the relevant backend implementation, tests and documentation. Torch is an optional dependency.

This change: includes focused unit tests. Validation scope is recorded below.

This change will: preserve the dependency scope described above.

## Motivation

Search workloads repeatedly compute batch peaks, sparse chi-square values and CPU FFTs; optional routes allow those costs to be optimized with explicit eligibility checks.

## Contents

Native batched peak and single-point chi-square kernels, guarded dispatch, and CPU FFT thread/plan tuning. This branch contains the two Cython additions excluded from the main stack and includes focused tuning and invalidation tests.

Baseline formatting is inherited through [main formatting prerequisite](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/18). The CPU follow-up needs no additional formatting prerequisite.

The optional CPU peak/chi-square kernels and native admission gate are preserved. CPU FFT tuning retains direct plans from 32768 through 524288 samples. The 1048576, 2097152 and 4194304 sample inverse FFTs use the qualified double-precision workspace only with one thread; other thread counts retain the fallback. New dispatch tests cover this integration. Native peak dispatch remains ahead of the improved Torch fallback inherited from [#15](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/15) at `2685db817fe0fdb77de2e0196fbdfd66d4faf713`. The later accelerator peak refinement leaves the CPU reduction algorithm unchanged. Inherited precision and executable-context fixes remain outside this PR’s own feature diff.

## Links to any issues or associated PRs

Depends on [#15](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/15) (`torch-pr11-performance-evidence`) at `2685db817fe0fdb77de2e0196fbdfd66d4faf713`. This optional CPU branch is independent of both optional FFT PRs.

Head branch: `torch-followup-cpu-optimizations`. Head commit: `fe0e15b275856128ed95dacc0a8b89f26d462118`. Base branch: `torch-pr11-performance-evidence`.

## Testing performed

Documentation cleanup: inherited final-versus-original results use one figure in one image directory. The 11 Torch pages pass a fresh warning-as-error Sphinx build, with deterministic figure regeneration. Runtime/test diffs and feature hunks are preserved; existing unit records retain their actual source identities. [Cleanup validation](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/0ffdcef424eecc151f28193133e00cf49d4e23b8/maintainer-documentation-20260906).

Publication head: `fe0e15b275856128ed95dacc0a8b89f26d462118`. Test and timing records below identify their actual source revisions. Verified patch preservation does not claim tests ran on a later publication commit.

The pre-cleanup optional CPU source passed 620 tests with 69 skips and 8 subtests across 28 files, plus qlty and the optional CPU documentation build. Integration checks cover one-thread admission and multi-thread fallback for all three promoted large inverse-FFT sizes. The native peak/chi-square kernels and native admission gate are preserved; the CPU feature integration and final lint cleanup are explicitly reviewed.

Sources: Pre-cleanup PR #17 tested source: `3e88711c1453d2ffab5eca42ec3207d34c50ddef`. Evidence: [Final source tests and lint](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/568f07197953c735a7ccbb666b0eed85d5561493/publication-qualification/quality-final-v6-r2/result.json), [Final #17 unit log](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/568f07197953c735a7ccbb666b0eed85d5561493/publication-qualification/quality-final-v6-r2/cpu-followup-units.log), [Final CPU integration tests](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/568f07197953c735a7ccbb666b0eed85d5561493/publication-qualification/quality-final-v6-r2/cpu-integration-final.json), [Optional CPU documentation build](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/568f07197953c735a7ccbb666b0eed85d5561493/publication-qualification/docs-validation-cpu-v6/docs-validation.json), [Reviewed final cleanup and identities](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/568f07197953c735a7ccbb666b0eed85d5561493/publication-qualification/publication/polish-proof-v6.json).

The historical optional CPU before/after campaign contains 36 worker processes, 12 standard controls and 24 passing parity comparisons. Both revisions enable PYCBC_TORCH_CPU_NATIVE_BATCH_PEAK=1 with native correlation and FFTW batch routing; admission may still fall back. This is synthetic matched-filter component throughput with vetoes, frame I/O, PSD estimation, bank loading and waveform generation excluded. It is distinct from the later full executable measurements and final publication tests.

Sources: Historical optional CPU before: `bd53914be6d2e4324cc867d52b3842b77cc6729a`; Historical optional CPU after: `1514327669fc7be125523b991c847868c3a2a17e`. Evidence: [Historical optional CPU comparison](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/639154f7ef359eb473db79660942a2cd88dd59e6/performance-fix/cpu-followup-report/report.json).

The optional CPU before/after comparison qualifies the recorded native-gate configuration and fallback; it does not change the preserved native CPU kernels.

Known CUDA limitation: immediate host reads can precede completion of non-blocking peak copies. A delayed-stream probe reproduced incorrect immediate arrays on both published and rebuilt PR5 heads; synchronization corrected all three arrays, while blocking copies were correct immediately. The implementation is byte-identical in those revisions. This race remains unresolved.

Comprehensive MPS qualification and a full-site Sphinx build are not claimed.

Historical evidence retains its original source and timing attribution: [commands, environment, source IDs and JUnit](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/7f1ea7a7aa05b4fdafe2995a43a754984a2c5817/batch1024/correctness); [Historical commands, JUnit and Qlty records](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/5c6c12d895fa7229fd0da2d10ade5ecfbae5153b/triton/restack-validation.json); [logs](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/5c6c12d895fa7229fd0da2d10ade5ecfbae5153b/triton/validation-logs); [six-batch CPU comparison](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/7f1ea7a7aa05b4fdafe2995a43a754984a2c5817); [Benchmark documentation](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/2685db817fe0fdb77de2e0196fbdfd66d4faf713/docs/torch_performance.rst); [figure manifest](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/2685db817fe0fdb77de2e0196fbdfd66d4faf713/docs/images/torch/manifest.json).
